title: Basavanna's Parliament of Souls
subtitle: When Work Became Worship and Words Became Fire
figure: Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi and Allama Prabhu
era: Kalachuri Kalyana and the vachana revolution, c. 1130-1196 CE
region: Basavana Bagewadi, Kudalasangama and Basavakalyana, Karnataka
moral: A just community lets every honest voice be heard.

sources.note: Near-contemporary Kannada account of Basavanna's circle.

sources.citation: Arjunavad inscription, 1260 CE, and Kalachuri-era records
sources.note: Epigraphic context for Basava's family and Bijjala's world.

sources.citation: A.K. Ramanujan, Speaking of Siva (1973); Jan Peter Schouten, Revolution of the Mystics (1991); R. Blake Michael, The Origins of Virasaiva Sects (1992)
sources.note: Translations and social-historical analysis of vachanas and Lingayat origins.

panels.shot: epic wide of a dim stone hall filled with shadowy figures sitting in a circle, with Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi and Allama Prabhu prominent in the foreground

dialogue.text: In twelfth‑century Kalyana, a king’s minister and wandering mystics dared to build a hall where cobbler, woman and Brahmin argued with God as equals: the remembered Anubhava Mantapa of Basavanna and his companions.

panels.shot: slow push-in on young Basavanna at a village field, low angle with horizon

dialogue.text: Basavanna was born in a small town of today’s Karnataka, where the dust of the fields and the smoke of the forges fed a boy who watched work and worship sit in different corners of the village.

panels.shot: medium wide of Kudalasangama river confluence at sunrise, contemplative framing

dialogue.text: At Kudalasangama, under the quiet gaze of stone shrines, he turned inward, taking the ishtalinga onto his own body, seeking a Lord who did not ask for birth-names or priestly fees.

panels.shot: interior wide of a royal court, with Basavanna small in the grand space

dialogue.text: The Arjunavad inscription and later memories place him in the court of Bijjala II at Kalyana, a minister handling royal wealth in a world where power sat with kings, Brahmins and guilds.

panels.shot: medium on Basavanna discreetly giving coins to a poor artisan outside the court gate

dialogue.text: From this seat near the treasury, Basavanna bent the flow of gifts: not only to temples but to hungry craftsmen and wandering devotees, turning royal coin toward a different kind of order.

panels.shot: intimate interior wide of a modest hall with Basavanna addressing a mixed group

dialogue.text: Here began what would be remembered as the Anubhava Mantapa: not a stone parliament, but a gathered experience, an assembly where weavers, potters, Brahmins and women shared their visions in plain Kannada.

panels.shot: close-up on Basavanna’s hands holding tools and the ishtalinga together

dialogue.text: In vachanas later remembered in Harihara’s ragales and Ramanujan’s pages, his voice made kayaka, one’s work, into worship, and the body’s labour into a temple that needed no caste-marked doorway.

panels.shot: dramatic entrance shot of Allama Prabhu into the hall, low angle with shadow

dialogue.text: From the caves and streets came others: Allama Prabhu, remembered as a drummer-ascetic, whose spare, riddling vachanas cut through pride, and who would sit at the heart of this debating circle.

panels.shot: medium on Allama and Basavanna sitting opposite, calm but intense

dialogue.speaker: basavanna_akka_mahadevi_and_allama_prabhu
dialogue.text: “Let the tongue speak only what the work has lived.”

panels.shot: wide shot of Akka Mahadevi entering the Mantapa, hair flowing, crowd reacting

dialogue.text: And Akka Mahadevi, whose life is sung in many later accounts, entered this remembered circle covered only by her hair and her devotion, her vachanas calling Shiva her only husband and earthly ties a distraction.

panels.shot: close-up on Akka Mahadevi’s intense face as she speaks, background softened

dialogue.speaker: basavanna_akka_mahadevi_and_allama_prabhu
dialogue.text: “Why bind the sky in a house of walls?”

panels.shot: dynamic wide of the Mantapa in full session, with diverse figures speaking in turn

dialogue.text: Within a generation, hundreds of sharanas—names preserved across the vachana collections—voiced their experience, arguing, contradicting, singing in Kannada prose-poems that carried the heat of the street into the language of God.

panels.shot: medium on Basavanna gently refusing a priestly ritual offering, with a small gathering watching

dialogue.text: Ishtalinga on their bodies, they loosened the old knots of temple and birth; yet even as they questioned Brahmin ritual, many still carried the habits of their world, and caste did not vanish from twelfth‑century Karnataka overnight.

panels.shot: tense interior of the court, with Brahmins and elites confronting Bijjala and Basavanna

dialogue.text: The king’s court, caught between revenue, ritual and revolt, heard complaints: that the minister’s circle ignored rank, that artisans dared debate Brahmins, that social walls were being thinned in the very capital.

panels.shot: somber wide of Kalyana streets with soldiers and frightened townsfolk, distant fires

dialogue.text: Traditions, hagiographies and history agree at least on this: tension rose. A royal order, a marriage across caste lines, a clash of loyalties—details differ, but by the late 1160s, Kalyana was no longer at peace.

panels.shot: medium of Basavanna leaving the city gate, looking back once

dialogue.text: Later Virashaiva memory tells that Basavanna left Kalyana and returned toward Kudalasangama, his experiment shaken by royal displeasure and conflict, his body’s path ending while his words travelled on.

panels.shot: poignant shot of Allama seated alone in a dim corner of the hall, the space half-empty
transitional montage wide of scribes and devotees across time copying vachanas

dialogue.text: Over the next centuries, their vachanas were gathered, edited and argued over; Virashaiva and Lingayat communities traced roots to them, while scholars still debate where Basavanna’s hand began and where older currents flowed in.

panels.shot: final wide shot of a modern gathering in a simple hall, faint silhouettes of Basavanna, Akka and Allama behind them

dialogue.text: In the remembered Parliament of Souls at Kalyana, they did not erase hierarchy in a day, but they dared to stage a different conversation—and each time we let a cobbler’s, a woman’s, a mystic’s voice stand, their Mantapa flickers back to life.
